domain: Risk Assessment / Energy Policy / Public Safety Governance
topic_summary: Analysis of the nuclear energy risk debate as a contested kernel where different parties read the acceptable-risk-for-energy commitment differently. The catastrophic-tail-dominant reading (anti-nuclear) weights low-probability high-consequence events heavily, emphasizing irreversibility and intergenerational burden. The expected-value-dominant reading (pro-nuclear) weights average annual costs and climate benefits, treating nuclear as quantifiable trade-off among energy alternatives.

key_entities: Nuclear Regulatory Bodies (IAEA, national regulators; authority grounded in probabilistic safety assessment)
Anti-Nuclear Movement (environmental advocacy; authority grounded in precautionary principle)
Nuclear Industry (operators, vendors; authority grounded in engineering expertise)
Historical Accidents (Chernobyl, Fukushima, TMI; empirical anchors for risk perception)
Radioactive Waste (multi-generational hazard; temporal scope beyond institutional lifespans)
Climate Change Mitigation Framework (competing existential risk; temporal urgency)
Affluent Educated White Males (demographic overrepresented in pro-nuclear position)
key_tensions: Asymmetric burden of proof: one accident proves danger, decades of safety prove nothing
Uncertainty quantification (PSA confidence intervals) vs uncertainty acknowledgment (irreducible unknowns)
Temporal framing: annual expected values vs multi-generational timescales
Competing risk comparisons: nuclear accidents vs coal emissions vs climate catastrophe
Institutional trust: industry/regulatory underestimation vs public skepticism
Intergenerational justice: waste disposal burden on future generations
key_mechanisms: Probabilistic Safety Assessment (PSA/PRA): quantifies failure probabilities and consequence severity; systematically underestimates cascade effects per historical record
Signal value amplification: any nuclear incident anywhere globally erodes trust in all nuclear programs
Heavy-tailed cost distribution: most years zero cost, rare years extreme cost driving total up
Defense-in-depth safety margin: compensates for PSA uncertainty by imposing strict redundancy
key_absences: Explicit framework for weighting intergenerational vs present-generation harm
Mechanism for adjudicating between competing existential risks (nuclear accident vs climate catastrophe)
Demographic analysis of who bears nuclear risk vs who benefits from energy production

axiom_contradictions.basis: Catastrophic-tail reading holds that irreversibility categorically dominates probability-weighted optimization; expected-value reading holds that all risks reduce to probability × consequence products. No single coherent framework weights both irreversibility as categorical constraint AND treats it as one factor in expected-value calculation.

Catastrophic-tail reading holds that intergenerational burden from waste creates absolute prohibition regardless of alternatives; comparative-risk reading holds that no energy risk is evaluable in isolation from competing risks. No single framework treats waste as absolute constraint AND as relative to climate catastrophe.

omegas.description: Can catastrophic-tail and expected-value readings coexist in policy (licensed plurality) or does one reading's adoption require suppressing the other? Current regulatory frameworks attempt hybrid (PSA + precautionary margins) but axiom contradiction suggests this is unstable.

Is the affluent-white-male overrepresentation in pro-nuclear position evidence of a Snare (those who decide bear less risk than those affected)? Deferred axis demographic_risk_tolerance_gap warrants independent analysis if spatial/demographic risk distribution is structurally central.
omegas.source: Deferred axis demographic_risk_tolerance_gap + Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan)

omegas.description: How do the three readings weight present vs future generations? Catastrophic-tail privileges future (waste burden), expected-value discounts future (climate urgency), comparative-risk treats as competing futures. No reading explicitly addresses intergenerational discount rate as independent variable.
omegas.source: Absence Inventory: explicit framework for weighting intergenerational vs present-generation harm

omegas.description: Is PSA underestimation a true Mountain (epistemic limits of modeling complex systems) or a Piton (correctable methodological choice)? If Mountain, expected-value reading's authority grounding collapses. If Piton, regulatory capture becomes the axis.
omegas.source: Deferred axis psa_underestimation_mountain + F03 (Hasty Generalization) concern

omegas.description: Comparative-risk reading assumes climate catastrophe and nuclear accident are commensurable risks. Are they? Different temporal profiles (gradual warming vs sudden meltdown), different reversibility (emissions cuts vs contamination), different victim sets. Absence of adjudication mechanism between existential risks.
omegas.source: Absence Inventory: mechanism for adjudicating between competing existential risks
